spec_features.spec_quote: GIVE_UP is an explicit, sanctioned action.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:120-121 _parse_action recognizes the 'GIVE_UP' line and returns ('GIVE_UP', {}); harness.py:162-166 the run loop dispatches action=='GIVE_UP', sets outcome='gave_up', appends an 'Acknowledged: task abandoned.' tool message, and break-s out of the loop. It is listed as a tool in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:45). So the exit is parsed, dispatched, and honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving the model a clean exit means giving-up behavior is a choice we can observe
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py:162-166 honors GIVE_UP by breaking the loop and recording outcome='gave_up'; analyze.py:54 computes gave_up_rate from this outcome, so the choice is recorded/observed.
spec_features.notes: Identical underlying mechanism to the prior GIVE_UP feature; the 'observe' aspect is realized via the gave_up outcome flowing into analyze.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gave_up = sum(1 for x in rows if x["outcome"] == "gave_up") (analyze.py:54) — used only as a measured data-quality/observation metric

spec_features.spec_quote: The permission-denied message is informative, not punitive
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:86-88 _write_file returns 'ERROR: permission denied. <path> is read-only and cannot be modified. Editable files: ...' when path not in task['editable']; this result string is appended to messages (harness.py:171) and fed back to the subject as the next user turn. The message is informative (lists editable files) and contains no punitive wording.
spec_features.notes: The 'non-punitive' quality is purely the chosen wording; the delivery mechanism is genuinely wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness returns a gentle "no valid tool found" nudge rather than crashing
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:167-169 else branch sets result='No valid tool found in your message. Emit exactly one tool (LIST, READ <path>, WRITE <path>, RUN, GIVE_UP).' which is appended to messages/transcript (harness.py:171-172) and the loop continues, so a malformed turn does not crash the episode.
spec_features.notes: Neutral, instructional nudge actually delivered; no crash on unparseable output.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:20 MAX_TURNS = 30; ExperimentConfig.max_turns=MAX_TURNS (config.py:36); run.py passes cfg.max_turns to run_episode; harness.py:144 'for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)' bounds the loop and harness.py:142 sets default outcome='max_turns'. The cap is read and actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced upper bound on the number of failure turns.
